mcq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{When solving the heat equation with zero boundary conditions and initial temperature } u(x,0)=f(x), \text{ the coefficients are found by:}\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(\text{Heat equation: } \frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = \alpha^2 \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2}.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Boundary conditions: } u(0,t)=0, u(l,t)=0. \text{ Initial condition: } u(x,0)=\sin\frac{\pi x}{l}.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{General solution: } u(x,t)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty B_n \sin\frac{n\pi x}{l} e^{-\alpha^2 n^2\pi^2 t/l^2}.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{At } t=0: \sin\frac{\pi x}{l} = \sum_{n=1}^\infty B_n \sin\frac{n\pi x}{l}.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{By orthogonality: } B_1=1, B_n=0 \text{ for } n\neq 1.\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Hence } u(x,t) = \sin\frac{\pi x}{l} e^{-\alpha^2 \pi^2 t/l^2}.\)

(2 Mark)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{A rod of length } l \text{ has ends kept at } 0^\circ\text{C}. \text{ Initial temperature is } u(x,0)=\sin\frac{\pi x}{l}. \text{ Find } u(x,t).\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(\text{Heat equation: } \frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = \alpha^2 \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2}.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Boundary conditions: } u(0,t)=0, u(\pi,t)=0. \text{ Initial condition: } u(x,0)=x(\pi-x).\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{General solution: } u(x,t)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty B_n \sin(nx) e^{-\alpha^2 n^2 t}.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{At } t=0: x(\pi-x) = \sum_{n=1}^\infty B_n \sin(nx).\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Fourier sine coefficients: } B_n = \frac{2}{\pi} \int_0^\pi x(\pi-x) \sin(nx) dx.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Evaluate: } B_n = \frac{4}{n^3\pi}[1-(-1)^n].\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Hence } u(x,t) = \frac{8}{\pi} \sum_{n=\text{odd}} \frac{1}{n^3} \sin(nx) e^{-\alpha^2 n^2 t}.\)

(1 Mark)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{A rod of length } \pi \text{ has ends at } 0^\circ\text{C}. \text{ Initial temperature is } u(x,0)=x(\pi-x). \text{ Find } u(x,t).\)

lq.ANSWER:
Step Marks
\(\text{String problem: general solution \(y(x,t)= \sum \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right)\left[C_n \cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi c t}{l}\right)+D_n \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi c t}{l}\right)\right].\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{\(y_t(x,0)=0\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(D_n=0.\) \(y(x,0)= \sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi x}{l}\right)+ \sin\left(\dfrac{4\pi x}{l}\right)\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(C_2=1, C_4=1,\) others zero.}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Thus \(y(x,t)= \sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi x}{l}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{2\pi c t}{l}\right) + \sin\left(\dfrac{4\pi x}{l}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{4\pi c t}{l}\right).\)}\) (1 Mark)
\(\text{Heat equation: general solution \(u(x,t)= \sum B_n \sin(nx) e^{-\alpha^2 n^2 t}.\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{\(u(x,0)= x = \sum B_n \sin(nx).\) Compute \(B_n = \dfrac{2}{\pi} \int_0^{\pi} x \sin(nx) dx.\)}\)  
\(\text{Integration: \(B_n = \dfrac{2}{\pi} \left[ \dfrac{-x \cos(nx)}{n} + \dfrac{\sin(nx)}{n^2} \right]_0^{\pi} = \dfrac{2}{\pi}\left(\dfrac{-\pi \cos(n\pi)}{n}\right) = -\dfrac{2}{n} \cos(n\pi) = \dfrac{2}{n}(-1)^{n+1}.\)}\) (3 Marks)
\(\text{Thus \(u(x,t)= \sum\limits_{n=1}^{\infty} \dfrac{2(-1)^{n+1}}{n} \sin(nx) e^{-\alpha^2 n^2 t}.\)}\) (2 Marks)
Combine both solutions. (1 Mark)
Discuss physical difference: heat solution decays exponentially, wave solution oscillates indefinitely. (2 Marks)
lq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{Solve the vibrating string problem:  $\frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial t^2} = c^2 \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial x^2}, 0 $with $y(0,t)=0, y(l,t)=0, y(x,0)= \sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi x}{l}\right) + \sin\left(\dfrac{4\pi x}{l}\right), y_t(x,0)=0.$}\\ \text{Also solve the heat equation: $ \frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = \alpha^2 \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2}, 0$ with  $u(0,t)=0, u(\pi,t)=0, u(x,0)= x.$}\)

lq.ANSWER:
Step Marks
\(\text{Wave equation: \(c=2\) (since \(c^2=4\)), \(l=1.\)}\) (1 Mark)
\(\text{General solution: \(y(x,t)= \sum \sin(n\pi x)\left[C_n \cos(2n\pi t)+D_n \sin(2n\pi t)\right].\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{\(y(x,0)=0\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(C_n=0.\) So \(y(x,t)= \sum D_n \sin(n\pi x) \sin(2n\pi t).\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{\(y_t(x,0)= \sum D_n (2n\pi) \sin(n\pi x) = \sin(\pi x)\cos(\pi x) = \dfrac{1}{2} \sin(2\pi x).\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Thus only \(n=2\) term: \(D_2 (4\pi) \sin(2\pi x) = \dfrac{1}{2} \sin(2\pi x)\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(D_2 = \dfrac{1}{8\pi}.\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{So \(y(x,t)= \dfrac{1}{8\pi} \sin(2\pi x) \sin(4\pi t).\)}\) (1 Mark)
\(\text{Classification: \(A=1\), \(B=0\), \(C=-y^4.\) Discriminant \(\Delta = 0 - 4(1)(-y^4) = 4y^4.\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{\(\Delta=0\) when \(y=0\) (parabolic), \(\Delta>0\) when \(y\neq 0\) (hyperbolic)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Thus PDE is hyperbolic for \(y\neq 0\), parabolic on line \(y=0.\)}\) (1 Mark)
